newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia regulator lists sharia approved stocks.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia regulator lists sharia approved stocks.

text.p: The Malaysian Securities Commission (SC) has released an initial list of 371 companies which have been deemed as religiously-acceptable or "halal" investments according to Islamic sharia laws.
In a statement sent out late on Wednesday, the market regulator said the list was approved by the Syariah Advisory Council of the SC.
The council came up with the list after analysing information including annual reports, responses to SC questionnaires and through discussions with officers of the companies, the statement said.
Under Islamic principles, "halal" companies cannot be involved in alcohol, gambling or other activities deemed to contradict Islamic laws.

The main board stocks list has 29 consumer products firms, 59 involved in industrial products, five in mining, 14 in construction, 25 in trading services, 23 in properties, 31 in plantations, two infrastructure project firms and two finance companies.
An additional 181 Second Board companies of small-capitalisation shares were also on the list.
